meta.title: Nepal · The 211 Files
meta.description: Nepal in The 211 Files: country, football origins, competitions, clubs, national team, current affairs and World Cup record.

sections.title: The country
sections.subtitle: A Himalayan state between India and China

paragraphs: Nepal is a landlocked nation between India and China, home to Everest and one of South Asia’s oldest nations. The modern country emerged in the 1700s, when Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha unified rival hill kingdoms and the Kathmandu Valley into a single Nepali state.

sections.title: Recent history
sections.subtitle: Royal authority, civil war and republic

paragraphs: Throughout the 20th century, Nepal struggled between royal authority and popular demands for democracy. This political tension was later deepened by a brutal civil war between 1996 and 2006.
In 2008, the monarchy was abolished and Nepal became a federal republic.

sections.title: Football origins
sections.subtitle: From palace circles to wider public interest

entries.heading: The game takes root
paragraphs: Football in Nepal traces its origins to 1921, when young Nepalis who had learned the sport abroad began playing it in Kathmandu.
At first football was closely linked to the palace environment, but it quickly attracted wider public attention.

sections.title: First competitions
sections.subtitle: The early cups, ANFA and the Martyr’s Memorial League

entries.heading: The first national landmarks
paragraphs: The earliest major competition was the Ram Janaki Cup, first held in 1934.
In 1947 King Tribhuvan established the Tribhuvan Challenge Shield, a knockout tournament.
ANFA was created in 1951, and the Martyr’s Memorial League was introduced in 1955.

sections.title: Main competitions
sections.subtitle: Kathmandu’s traditional league and the wider National League

cards.title: Martyr’s Memorial A-Division League
cards.text: The Martyr’s Memorial A-Division League is Nepal’s traditional top tier. No team from outside the Kathmandu Valley has ever played in it. The competition is currently on hiatus.

cards.title: National League
cards.text: The National League was introduced to broaden top-level football outside the capital area and give clubs from beyond the Kathmandu Valley a national platform.

sections.title: Main clubs
sections.subtitle: Manang Marsyangdi, Three Star and Nepal Police

cards.title: Manang Marsyangdi Club
cards.text: Manang Marsyangdi is one of Nepal’s traditional football giants and a central name in the Kathmandu club game.

cards.title: Three Star Club
cards.text: Three Star is another of Nepal’s major traditional clubs and one of Manang Marsyangdi’s principal domestic rivals.

cards.title: Nepal Police Club
cards.text: Mahendra Police—now Nepal Police—produced the country’s best AFC club run, reaching the 2007 President’s Cup final. This competition is a third-tier Asian tournament comparable in concept to the UEFA Conference League.

sections.title: National team
sections.subtitle: From irregular early matches to the Solidarity Cup

entries.heading: FIFA membership and official debut
paragraphs: Although Nepal played irregularly in the 1960s, ANFA entered FIFA in 1972.
Nepal’s first official match was played against China on 13 October 1972.

entries.heading: The strongest spell
paragraphs: Nepal’s best spell came in the mid-2010s. The national team won the 2016 AFC Solidarity Cup and also collected regional honours at youth and South Asian Games level.

entries.heading: Third-party interference
paragraphs: ANFA is in turmoil. A dispute over its district-based electoral structure led Nepal’s National Sports Council to intervene in the federation’s election process.
FIFA judged that intervention to constitute third-party interference and suspended ANFA from international football.
